chapter_theme: The opening of Konganar's Valaik Kummi, a women's clapping-dance song addressed to the Maiden (வாலை), the young goddess who is at once Shakti, the power at the root of the body and the flame in the lamp. After seven invocations the song claims that she, without mother or father, made earth and sky, and that the five letters (அஞ்செழுத்து) made the world, the soul and the ages; the mute letter is the body and Om is the life, and the unseen can be seen by meditating on the five rather than by reading sastra and Veda. The chapter ends by turning from the open word to cipher and from the filthy body to the lamp that burns above the crown.
structure_note: 1864 to 1870 are invocations (a venba to Vinayaka, then kummi stanzas to Vinayaka, Saraswati, Siva, Murugan, Vishnu and Nandi), each naming the Maiden under a different epithet; 1871 to 1874 announce the song and its subject, how world, Veda, gods and the Maiden arose; 1875 to 1883 are on the five letters, Om and the mute letter; 1884 and 1885 on the Chidambara chakra and the firm mind; 1886 to 1888 turn to cipher, the body and the lamp above the crown. The refrain வாலைப்பெண்ணே begins at 1871 and is not present in every stanza.

1864.reading: To tell this kummi on the Lady whom the learned call the Maiden full of learning, their beloved, we set in the heart the lotus feet of the one who excels the wise and whose word is sweet to the gods.
1864.nuance: A venba invocation, not a kummi stanza. The second half (நல்விசய நாதனின்சொல் வேதனஞ்சு போதன்மிஞ்சி மானகஞ்ச பாதம்வஞ்ச நெஞ்சினில்) is run together and partly garbled; the god addressed is Vinayaka by the section heading, and வஞ்ச நெஞ்சு (deceitful heart) seems to be the poet's own.

1865.reading: Shakti, who bears the matted locks, is the Maiden; to tell the kummi on that excellent one, the one-tusked Siddhi Vinayaka who helped in the art is our protection.
1865.nuance: சடாதரி (bearer of matted hair) gives the Maiden an ascetic Siva-like form; வித்தைக்கு உதவிய (who helped the art) makes Vinayaka the patron of the song's craft.

1866.reading: The Maiden whom the Siddhars praise is that Shakti; to tell the kummi on her, the golden feet of Saraswati, the wife who dances to the drum's beat, are our protection.
1866.nuance: சித்தர்கள் போற்றிய names the Maiden as the Siddhars' own goddess, which is the song's claim throughout. தத்தமித்தோம் is a drum-syllable string, placing Saraswati in the dance.

1867.reading: The Maiden is she who fills everything, Vishnu's younger sister; to sing the kummi on her, the lotus feet of Siva Sambhu who wears the Ganga, the true guru, are our protection.
1867.nuance: எங்கும் நிறைந்தவள் gives the goddess the pervasion usually predicated of Siva. Siva is invoked as சற்குரு, the true guru, which is how the Siddhars take him.

1868.reading: She is the woman of knowledge, the woman of the light of grace, the primal Maiden; to sing the kummi on her, Murugan, who made the deer a woman and who suits Valli, is our protection.
1868.nuance: மானைப் பெண்ணாக்கிய refers to Valli, born of a deer in her legend; the epithets ஞானப்பெண், அருள்சோதிப்பெண் make the Maiden knowledge and light before she is a person.

1869.reading: She is the beggar-woman and the royal Pandya woman, the Maiden Ambika; to sing the kummi on her, the golden feet of the lord of Vaikuntha, who took up the service of the Gandiva-bearer, are our protection.
1869.nuance: ஆண்டிப்பெண் is the wife of the beggar Siva and ராசபாண்டிப்பெண் the Pandya princess, Meenakshi of Madurai; the two epithets give the goddess both poverty and royalty. காண்டீபனாம் பணி பூண்டவன் is read as Krishna who served Arjuna as charioteer, so the god is Vishnu.

1870.reading: Antari and Sundari are the Maiden; to sing the kummi on that Ambika, the golden feet of Nandi, who comes first into the thought as a fine wonder, are our protection.
1870.nuance: Nandi here is the guru of the Siddhar lineage, as in the Tirumanthiram, rather than the bull. அந்தரி (she of the inner space) carries the yogic sense beside the name.

1871.reading: On the Maiden, the able one who danced within bounds at Thillai and at Mullai, to sing the sporting kummi in Tamil removes old karma.
1871.nuance: The dancer at Thillai is Siva in the Saiva tradition; the song gives the dance to the Maiden. சல்லாபக் கும்மி, the sporting kummi, names the genre as play, and the claim that singing it removes karma is the song's warrant for itself.

1872.reading: Without mother or father, in the open space, to make earth and sky, the innocent girl, the first Maiden, entered as its ruler; this world is contained in her.
1872.nuance: மாதா பிதா கூட இல்லாமல் makes her unborn and so beginningless, which the Siddhars elsewhere ask of the letter and the soul. பேதைப்பெண் (innocent girl) and the ruler of the world are the same person: the Maiden is young and supreme at once.

1873.reading: How the Veda and the elements arose, how space became science and sastra, how nada and song arose: listen, I will tell the way.
1873.nuance: The stanza is a table of contents: Veda, elements, sciences and sound are all to be derived. வெளி (space) as the source of the sciences is the Siddhar cosmology in which all comes from the void.

1874.reading: How the three worlds arose, how the first god and the gods arose, and how, wondrously, the Maiden arose: see this exposition of knowledge.
1874.nuance: The Maiden too has an arising (வாலை உண்டானது), though 1872 made her unparented; the song does not reconcile the two. ஞான விளக்கம் is both exposition and lamp of knowledge, the image taken up at 1888.

1875.reading: What preceded Hari is the letter A; what stood within Hari is the five letters; what preceded holding is the five letters; and what stood within the breath-horse is the five letters.
1875.nuance: The stanza turns on அரி, which is Hari, Vishnu, but in cipher can be the sun or the letter; வாசிப்பரி is the horse that is the breath. Tradition takes the stanza to place the five letters in the breath, so that the mantra is breathed rather than said. தரிக்கும் (holding, or bearing) is unclear.

1876.reading: In the beginning the Maiden became the five letters and took the name five letters; she is not the mute letter of the nadi; she became the way of knowledge itself.
1876.nuance: நாதியின் ஊமை எழுத்து is unclear: நாதி may be a corrupt நாடி (channel) or an echo of நாதம் (sound). The stanza distinguishes the Maiden from the mute letter that 1877 then makes the body, so she is the sounded five, not the silent one.

1877.reading: The mute letter became the body, and the letter Om became the life; know this letter and dance the kummi in play.
1877.nuance: ஊமை எழுத்து, the mute letter, is in tradition the unsounded letter beyond the fifty-one, sometimes the half-letter of Om; here it is assigned to the body and the sounded Om to the life. Sangili Siddhar reverses the assignment (2111).

1878.reading: What created the world is the five letters; what created the soul is the five letters; what ended the age is the five letters; and what made it arise again is the five letters.
1878.nuance: Creation, destruction and re-creation of the age (உகம்) are all given to the mantra, which stands here for Siva's acts, as in Tirumular's chapter on the five letters.

1879.reading: What if you have looked at the sastras, what if you have looked at the Veda too? It is the formula you must see and master; it is by knowing the five words that you must see.
1879.nuance: சூத்திரம் (sutra, formula, also the puppet-string) is set against the books: knowing the five letters is the thread that works the rest. The dismissal of scripture is mild beside Sivavakkiyar's; the Veda is useless only without the five.

1880.reading: If you think the five are not seen, not gained, not reached, and nothing comes of them, know that by the five letters the unseen can be seen, and there is effect in them if you meditate.
1880.nuance: The stanza answers a doubter in his own words (காணாது கிட்டாதே எட்டாதே) and makes meditation, not recitation, the condition of the letters' effect.

1881.reading: The cowherd is within the fifth letter; the knowing one is within the fifth letter; the speaking one is within the fifth letter; and this Maiden is within the fifth letter.
1881.nuance: ஐந்தாம் எழுத்து may be the fifth letter (in சிவாயநம, ம or ய) or the five letters together. ஆயன் is Krishna, the cowherd; அறிவாயன் and வாயன் are read as the knower and the speaker, but may be further names of gods. The stanza places god, knower and Maiden in one letter.

1882.reading: The five letters became eight letters, and then the fifty-one syllables; will you know the truth that stands by the letter of the heart, Maiden?
1882.nuance: Five, eight and fifty-one are the Siva pancakshara, the eight-letter mantra (ஓம் நமசிவாய with its seeds, or the Vishnu ashtakshara) and the full alphabet; Pattinathar names the same three (659). நெஞ்செழுத்து (heart-letter) is unclear: the letter held in the heart, or a letter that is the heart. நிலையாமல் is corrupt for நிலையான or நிலையாம்.

1883.reading: The five letters deceive and wear away; reach out and grasp the two letters; watch the breath and, above, see the state of the breath, Maiden.
1883.nuance: ஏய்க்குது தேய்க்குது (it deceives, it wears) is a strange thing to say of the five letters; the stanza may mean the spoken five fail and the two (tradition says சி and வ, or the in and out breath, or அ and உ) are to be held. வாசியை மேலாக (the breath above) points to the raised breath at the crown. The first line's metre is broken.

1884.reading: The great ones in this land know the Chidambara chakra; but if it is the Chidambara chakra, you must know the deity within it.
1884.nuance: The plain reading is of the drawn yantra of Chidambaram, known to the learned; the coded reading, following Tirumular's claim that the body is Chidambaram, makes the chakra the body and the deity the Maiden within it. The stanza rebukes those who know the diagram but not what it holds.

1885.reading: If there is no mind and intellect, what can she do, though she tells of changing the way? One must keep firmness of mind, and then the Maiden's grace must come.
1885.nuance: Grace is set after effort: the goddess cannot help a mind that will not hold. வழி மாறுதல் (changing the way) is read as the turning of the breath or the way of life; the stanza does not say which.

1886.reading: I will not say it in the open any more; you with lined eyes, sweet-voiced women, come here, and I will tell you a little of the core; listen.
1886.nuance: வெளியினில் சொல்லாதே announces the turn from plain speech to cipher, and கரு (the core, the embryo) is what follows. The second line, தீமட்டு திந்தவரி விழிக்கே, is corrupt; it seems to address the women by their painted eyes.

1887.reading: Do not think this a filthy corpse; do not think it a salted pot; for those who have seen there is no filth in it; look at it within your own body.
1887.nuance: The stanza turns against the Siddhars' own stock images of the body (ஊத்தைச் சடலம், உப்பிட்ட பாண்டம், the salted pot that will not last): the body is foul only to those who have not seen what it holds. It is the premise of the body-map that follows in the next chapter.

1888.reading: Straight above the crown, above the uvula, a lamp set there burns daily; the lamp with an axis is the Maiden, and it burns without going out, Maiden.
1888.nuance: உச்சிக்கு நேராய் உண்ணாக்குக்கு மேல் places the lamp at the crown above the palate, where tradition puts the thousand-petalled centre and the Maiden as the flame in the wick. அச்சுள்ள விளக்கு (the lamp with an axis or pivot) is unclear; a hanging or turning lamp, or the lamp that is the axis of the body.

links.note: Konganar makes the mute letter the body and Om the life; Sangili Siddhar, in the same kummi diction, makes the Omkara circle the body and the mute letter the life. Read as assignments of the two letters to body and life, the two stanzas contradict each other; read as saying only that both letters make the person, they agree.

Tirumular says that by the five letters the Lord made the five elements, the wombs of birth and the world; Konganar says the five letters created the world and the soul and ended and restarted the age. Both give the mantra the Lord's own acts, Konganar without naming the Lord.

Pattinathar praises the Lord who stands as the five letters, the eight letters and the fifty-one syllables; Konganar's stanza has the same three counts in the same order, as stages of the letters' growth. The shared triad shows a fixed Siddhar formula.

Tirumular runs the letters downward: the fifty letters are the Vedas and Agamas and, known, become the five. Konganar runs them upward: five become eight and then fifty-one. The two are the same correspondence read in opposite directions, contraction toward the mantra against expansion from it.

Tirumular says the human body is the Sivalinga, Chidambaram, Sadasiva and the dance; Konganar says those who know the Chidambara chakra must know the deity within it. On the coded reading, the chakra is the body and the deity the Maiden within it, which is Tirumular's claim applied to the goddess.

Sangili Siddhar tells the woman that this is a filthy corpse, a salted pot and a leather bellows to be crossed; Konganar tells her not to think it a filthy corpse or a salted pot, since for those who have seen there is no filth in it. The same two stock phrases are affirmed in one song and denied in the other; the conflict holds if the body is the same thing in both and not a gross body against a subtle one.

The Naladiyar calls the body a pot that seeps filth from nine openings, admired only by a fool dazzled by its skin; Konganar says those who have seen find no filth in it and should look within it. The conflict holds on the plain reading: for the Naladiyar seeing the body truly is seeing its filth, for Konganar it is seeing past the filth to what it holds.

source_issues: 1864 is a venba, not a kummi stanza, and its second half is run together without word division (வேதனஞ்சு போதன்மிஞ்சி மானகஞ்ச பாதம்வஞ்ச); the sense is partly lost.
1882: நிலையா மலந்த is corrupt, probably for நிலையான அந்த.
1883: the first line ஏய்க்கு தேய்க்கு ஐந்செழுத் துவதை is metrically short and ஐந்செழுத்து is a misspelling of ஐந்தெழுத்து or அஞ்செழுத்து.
1886: the second line தீமட்டு திந்தவரி விழிக்கே is corrupt.
The refrain வாலைப்பெண்ணே appears in 1871, 1873, 1874, 1882 and 1883 only; the other stanzas end on their own fourth line.
